sections.h2: Who sets and collects property tax in Flint, Michigan?
sections.html:
In Flint the city's Assessments Division sets the value of each parcel and the city bills the tax, while the Genesee County Treasurer takes over any bill still unpaid after the city collection period ends. Each office has its own phone line and its own forms, so it pays to know which one you need.

The Assessments Division keeps the record on every parcel, from land and buildings to property transfer affidavits, principal residence exemptions, land splits and combinations. The county equalization office keeps parcel descriptions for the rest of Genesee County but not for Flint, so a Flint question about acreage, a split or a lot line starts at city hall. The assessor's phone number on the city page is 810-766-7255.

  • Value and exemptions: City of Flint Assessments Division, 810-766-7255.
  • Current bills: City of Flint, which accepts property tax payments online through InvoiceCloud from its online services page. A BS&A portal on the same page lets you look up a parcel.
  • Delinquent bills: Genesee County Treasurer, 324 S Saginaw St Ste 2A, open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about homes in Flint?
sections.html:
Flint is a small, low-priced housing market sitting inside a much larger county. The Census Bureau counts 79,306 people in the city for July 2025, down from 81,252 in 2020 and 102,434 in 2010. The city covers 33.44 square miles of land along the Flint River, about 66 miles northwest of Detroit.

The history explains the housing stock. A trading post went up at a ford of the river in 1819, the city was incorporated in 1855, and General Motors was founded in Flint in 1908. GM's local workforce fell from about 80,000 in 1978 to under 8,000 by 2010, and the city's population dropped from 196,940 in 1960 to 102,434 in 2010. Many owners now carry houses worth far less than they once were.

sections.h2: How does Flint decide what my house is worth for tax?
sections.html:
The city estimates true cash value from two years of sales and market data, then places the assessed value on the roll at 50% of that figure. Michigan taxes a separate number called taxable value, which can never exceed the assessed value.

Taxable value is where a sale matters. The year after a property changes hands, taxable value jumps up to match assessed value, which Flint's assessor calls uncapping. The city's own example shows a 2025 taxable value of $25,114 against an assessed value of $60,000, and after an October 2025 sale the 2026 taxable value became $65,000. From the second year after the purchase, growth is limited again to the inflation rate multiplier or 5%, whichever is lower, absent new construction.

For a seller this matters in two ways. The tax bill you have been paying may be lower than the one your buyer will receive, and a buyer who escrows taxes should expect the lender to raise the monthly payment. Telling a buyer about uncapping up front avoids a bad surprise after closing.

sections.h2: When can a Flint owner appeal an assessment?
sections.html:
Flint owners can protest a value only at the March Board of Review. The Notice of Assessment goes out at the end of February and carries the meeting dates; it states at the top that it is not a tax bill.

The 2026 March board met on March 9, March 10 and March 12, and its decisions are final for that year. After the board closes, the city says the assessment office has no legal authority to change the value. Commercial and industrial owners can go straight to the Michigan Tax Tribunal by May 31. For residential property the statute sets a July 31 filing date for a tribunal petition in the tax year involved, and it requires the owner to have protested to the board first. The city's 2024 notice also allowed a notarized letter with original signatures and supporting documents in place of a visit, so ask the assessor how the current year works.

  • Poverty and hardship exemption: Flint's online services page lists a homeowner poverty and hardship application, called HOPE.
  • Disabled veteran exemption: an affidavit goes to the assessor with an explanation of benefits.
  • Principal residence exemption: the home must be owned and occupied by June 1, and it removes 18 mills of school operating tax. File a rescission when you move out, because a missed rescission can lead to a denial with penalties.

sections.h2: What are Flint's property tax due dates?
sections.html:
Use the due dates printed on your Flint bill, because the city bills on its own schedule and the bill controls. Ask the City of Flint if you did not receive one.

Two state rules sit behind the city's calendar. Summer tax is a lien from July 1, and a summer tax collected with city taxes carries the same penalties as the city's other taxes. Whatever is still unpaid on March 1 goes to the Genesee County Treasurer as delinquent, with a 4% county fee and interest of 1% per month added from that date.

sections.h2: What happens when Flint property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
The county takes the parcel through a three-year process that ends with a court judgment and an auction. The state timeline below is the one Genesee County follows.

  • First March 1: unpaid tax is returned to the county treasurer, and the 4% fee and monthly interest start.
  • Second March 1: the parcel forfeits to the treasurer, a $175 title fee is added, and redemption interest of half a percent a month runs from the March 1 before forfeiture.
  • March 30 and 31 of the next year: the circuit court must enter a judgment of foreclosure by March 30, and March 31 is the last day to redeem. Title then vests in the county.
  • Summer and fall: agencies get a first right of refusal, then online auctions follow. Genesee County held its 2026 rounds on September 3, September 25 and October 30.

The county treasurer's page also describes a class settlement over surplus proceeds from foreclosure sales between 2013 and 2020, with a claims deadline of July 16, 2026 that has passed. Anyone who lost a Flint house to tax foreclosure should ask the treasurer's office what remedies remain.

sections.h2: What does selling a Flint house with tax due look like?
sections.html:
You can sell a Flint house that owes tax, and the unpaid amount is normally paid from your proceeds at the closing table. The title company asks the city or the county treasurer for a payoff figure that includes interest and fees to the closing date.

A few closing costs belong to the seller by statute. Michigan's state transfer tax is $3.75 per $500 of value, and the county tax is 55 cents per $500 in a county of fewer than two million people, which includes Genesee. The seller is liable, and the tax goes to the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed is delivered. On a $60,000 sale that works out to $450 state and $66 county. Transfers on foreclosure, deeds to a child or grandchild, and land contracts that keep title with the seller are among the exemptions the statute lists.

Two city filings come along with a sale. The buyer or seller files a property transfer affidavit with Flint's assessor after the transfer, and a seller who claimed the principal residence exemption files a rescission. If back tax, repairs or a tenant are making a traditional listing hard, a cash buyer who takes the house as-is lets the payoff come out of the closing in one step.

faqs.q: Who do I pay property tax to in Flint?
faqs.a: Pay the City of Flint for current bills, online through InvoiceCloud or by the methods printed on the bill. Once taxes are returned as delinquent on March 1, payment goes to the Genesee County Treasurer at 324 S Saginaw St Ste 2A.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Flint assessment after the March board closes?
faqs.a: Not for a residential parcel, because the city's value becomes final when the March Board of Review closes. Commercial and industrial owners can petition the Michigan Tax Tribunal directly by May 31.

faqs.q: Will my Flint taxes go up after I buy a house?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Taxable value uncaps to the assessed value the year after a sale, then growth is limited to the inflation multiplier or 5%, whichever is lower. The city's assessor suggests contacting your lender if taxes are escrowed.

faqs.q: Does the buyer inherit my unpaid Flint property tax?
faqs.a: Unpaid tax is a lien on the parcel under state law, so it has to be settled for the buyer to receive clean title. In a normal sale the title company pays it from the seller's proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: Who pays transfer tax when a Flint house sells?
faqs.a: The seller is liable under both the state and county transfer tax laws. The state rate is $3.75 per $500 and the Genesee County rate is 55 cents per $500, paid to the county treasurer within 15 days of delivering the deed.
